items.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview
items.q: There's Ernie Wilkins, good arranger. Quincy Jones is another. But he has to have the type of caliber musician to play it.

ctx.x: And he's a beautiful musician, you know? But then you catch a cat that can write all kind of music, you know, all kind of -- I'll use the old term -- snakes and turns and

twists, brilliant. But he's got to have somebody to interpret his ideas. He's got to have somebody that can play his music, you know. There's Ernie Wilkins, good arranger. Quincy Jones is another. But he has to have the type of caliber musician to play it. It's like I say, Duke. Duke would write something for Johnny, because Johnny knew how to play it, you know. He couldn't write out the solo that Johnny would play, but Johnny would interpret his idea.
Interpret that in the way that he wanted.
